key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: Combining detonation spraying with laser remelting offers a promising route to wear-resistant nickel-based coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel components.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC coatings by detonation spraying, then laser remelt.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: After remelting, hardness rose from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, friction coefficient fell from 0.535 to 0.409, and specific wear rate decreased from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Remelting reduced coating thickness, so dimensional allowance requires attention; corrosion current density improved only modestly, by approximately 3%.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
